SOCIAL STUDIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which item usually comes last on an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. Opening prayer
   B. Closing remarks
   C. Reading of minutes
   D. Reports

2. What is a motto? (1 mark)
   A. A class register
   B. A school bag
   C. A short sentence showing what a school stands for
   D. A school bell

3. Which cloth is a printed cloth worn especially at the Kenyan coast? (1 mark)
   A. Kanga
   B. Suit
   C. Shuka
   D. Jeans

4. Which action shows cleanliness? (1 mark)
   A. Putting litter in the bin
   B. Writing on walls
   C. Spitting in class
   D. Throwing rubbish on the ground

5. Why are mountains important for water? (1 mark)
   A. They stop all rain
   B. They catch rain and give rise to rivers
   C. They make the land flat
   D. They dry up lakes

6. Which of these is a religious leader? (1 mark)
   A. A farmer
   B. A pastor
   C. A driver
   D. A trader

7. Why was Fort Jesus built? (1 mark)
   A. To keep cattle
   B. To make sugar
   C. To guard the harbour
   D. To grow food

8. Where is titanium mined in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Nyeri
   B. Kisumu
   C. Kwale
   D. Nakuru

9. What does fairness mean? (1 mark)
   A. Favouring rich people
   B. Favouring friends
   C. Ignoring people
   D. Treating everyone equally

10. A pupil says that a county with many people must be the biggest in area. What is wrong with this idea? (1 mark)
   A. Area and population are different things
   B. Only farms make counties big
   C. People make land bigger
   D. Counties never have people

11. Which of these is a Maasai red or blue checked cloth? (1 mark)
   A. Uniform
   B. Kikoi
   C. Shuka
   D. Kanga

12. What is a budget? (1 mark)
   A. A type of tool
   B. A crop
   C. A plan of how much money you expect to spend and earn
   D. A game

13. In a shaded map, which shade usually shows the most crowded area? (1 mark)
   A. No shade
   B. The lightest shade
   C. White
   D. The darkest shade

14. Which direction is Nakuru from Nairobi? (1 mark)
   A. East
   B. South-east
   C. North-west
   D. South

15. What does interdependence mean? (1 mark)
   A. People living alone
   B. People needing and helping each other
   C. People doing everything themselves
   D. People fighting

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Describe how you would prepare for a class visit to a museum, and what you would do during the visit. (5 marks)

17. Explain the meaning of population distribution. (2 marks)

18. Explain why herding communities live in sparsely populated areas. (3 marks)

19. Explain why we should be honest even when nobody is watching. (3 marks)

20. Explain the meaning of democracy. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Closing remarks
   Meetings end with closing remarks.

2. C — A short sentence showing what a school stands for
   A motto is a short saying of aims.

3. A — Kanga
   The kanga is printed cloth popular on the coast.

4. A — Putting litter in the bin
   Using bins keeps the school clean.

5. B — They catch rain and give rise to rivers
   Mountains catch rain and feed rivers.

6. B — A pastor
   Pastors lead worship.

7. C — To guard the harbour
   It was built as a stone fort to guard the harbour.

8. C — Kwale
   Titanium is mined in Kwale County.

9. D — Treating everyone equally
   Fair people give everyone equal treatment.

10. A — Area and population are different things
   Size is about area. Population is the number of people.

11. C — Shuka
   The shuka is a checked cloth worn by the Maasai.

12. C — A plan of how much money you expect to spend and earn
   A budget plans money.

13. D — The darkest shade
   Dark shades show higher numbers.

14. C — North-west
   Nakuru is north-west of Nairobi.

15. B — People needing and helping each other
   Interdependence means we depend on each other.

SECTION B
----
16. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission from the teacher and the museum, prepare questions, take a notebook, stay with the group, listen to the guide, take notes and do not touch objects.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point, up to 5.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is how the people are spread out over an area, showing where many people live and where few live.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for spread of people, 1 mark for many and few.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: The land is dry, so it cannot support many farms. Herders move with their animals to look for water and grass. So only a few people stay in one place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty builds trust, it is right, and it prepares us to be good citizens.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: Democracy is rule by the people, where everyone has a say in choosing leaders and making decisions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rule by the people, 1 mark for having a say.
